deities: Goddess Kasar Devi (a local form of Durga/Katyayani); a second group of shrines is dedicated to Shiva and Bhairav
festivals: Kasar Fair (Kartik Purnima; thousands of devotees attend)

history.dynasty: None documented (ancient shrine; local legend credits later patronage by the Katyuri kings)
history.period: 2nd century CE (widely repeated in tourism sources; archaeological backing is weak - verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is at Kasar Devi village on the Kaashay Hills, ~8 km from Almora town (not in Almora itself); documented with the corrected location. Dedicated to Goddess Kasar Devi, the shrine's present structure is conventionally dated to the 2nd century CE. Tradition from the Skanda Purana and Devi Bhagavata says the goddess Kaushiki defeated the demons Shumbh and Nishumbh here. In 1890 Swami Vivekananda meditated here and recorded deep spiritual experiences; Buddhist teacher Lama Anagarika Govinda also practised meditation at the site. In the 1960s-70s it became a focal point of the hippie movement, drawing seekers including Allen Ginsberg, Timothy Leary and Bob Dylan to nearby Crank's Ridge (Hippie Hill). Popular sources place the hill in a 'Van Allen Belt' geomagnetic zone alongside Machu Picchu and Stonehenge - a widely repeated claim without scientific consensus; NASA is said to have marked GPS gravity study points on the premises. The complex holds two groups of temples (Devi; Shiva-Bhairav) with an Akhand Jyoti burning around the clock.

name: Kasardevi Temple
town: Kasar Devi, Almora district (CSV town 'Almora' is imprecise - the temple is ~8 km from Almora town on the Binsar Road)
town_description: Kasar Devi is a small ridge village on the pine-covered Kaashay Hills at ~2,116 m, about 8 km from Almora. Named for its temple, it is famed for 360-degree views of the Nanda Devi and Trishul ranges, the Crank's Ridge hippie-era settlement, and its calm atmosphere that has drawn meditators and artists for over a century.

travel.airport: Pantnagar Airport (~124 km from Kasar Devi per one travel guide); road onward via Almora
travel.railway: Kathgodam railway station (~88 km per one guide; ~83 km per another - verify), then road to Almora and on to Kasar Devi
travel.road: 8 km from Almora town on the Binsar Road by taxi or local bus; the final approach is a steep ~500 m climb of 100-150 stone steps

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November; the Kartik Purnima fair is the festive high point
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-7:00 PM per chardhamtours.in (entry free); one listing cites different hours - verify locally
